title: Fix crash on closed generic structs from referenced assemblies

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.intent: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly must build cleanly and still get a generated resolver.

functional.text: The generator does not throw when a member's type is a closed generic struct or record struct defined in a referenced assembly.
The analyzer does not throw for the same member types.
The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project.

nonFunctional.text: A failure of the generator or analyzer must not pass silently as a build warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. (inferred)
Behaviour for generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same project does not change. (inferred)

story.what: TypeCollector now wraps the analyzer's diagnostic callback so that it only reports diagnostics whose location is in a syntax tree of the compilation being analyzed. Two places that indexed DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] now use a safe lookup. These are the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull property diagnostic, through the new GetPropertyIdentifierLocation helper, and the MemberNeedsKey field diagnostic, through FirstOrDefault. Metadata-only members no longer index an empty array. The change also flips the comparison that sets nonPublicMembersAreSerialized for keyed properties. Three new tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata image and run the analyzers and generator against a consuming project. The README and the MsgPack004 docs describe how diagnostics work for types from referenced assemblies.
story.why: Issue 2283 (MP-2283): the generator and analyzer threw IndexOutOfRangeException when a [MessagePackObject] member's type was a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly. These members have no source declarations, so DeclaringSyntaxReferences is empty. The crash showed up as a CS8785 or AD0001 warning and left the assembly without a generated resolver.

findings.title: Keyed-property accessibility check inverted, flags every public keyed member
findings.detail: In GetObjectInfo, the keyed-property branch now sets nonPublicMembersAreSerialized when the property is public (== Accessibility.Public). The comment above it and the matching field branch at line 1120 still use !=. Nothing in the requirement asks for this. In practice, any ordinary [MessagePackObject] type with a public [Key] property is now treated as serializing non-public members. In analyzer mode, line 1352 then reports MessagePackObjectAllowPrivateRequired on fully public types, and deferred non-public-member diagnostics get reported. In both analyzer and generator mode, the partial-type check at line 1382 now runs for types whose only issue is a private setter, so their formatter is dropped (return null) when the type is not partial. This breaks N2: existing analyzer tests and snapshots will change. The new metadata-reference tests should also fail, because MyObject has a public keyed property and the test expects no diagnostics.

findings.title: Filter silently drops in-project diagnostics that have no location
findings.detail: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation forwards a diagnostic only when its location is in source. Many diagnostics for types declared in the project are built with locations that can be null, for example FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax() or the new GetPropertyIdentifierLocation. Those diagnostics are now dropped instead of being reported without a location. One concrete case: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation only handles PropertyDeclarationSyntax. For a positional record property declared in the project, the declaring syntax is a ParameterSyntax, so the helper returns null and BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull is lost silently. Line 926 already handles ParameterSyntax for MemberNeedsKey; the helper does not. This changes analyzer behaviour for in-project types, which N2 says must not change.

citations.quote: var identifier = (syntax as PropertyDeclarationSyntax)?.Identifier ?? (syntax as ParameterSyntax)?.Identifier;

findings.title: No check of generated resolver content or runtime round trip
findings.detail: F3 requires the consuming assembly to get a working resolver and formatter, as it does for same-project generics. The new tests skip the generated-sources check and only assert that a resolver hint name exists. Nothing checks that the resolver registers a formatter for the cross-assembly closed generic struct, or that serialize and deserialize work through it. A resolver that is empty or wrong would still pass.

findings.title: Generator or analyzer failures can still pass as build warnings
findings.detail: N1 asks that a generator or analyzer failure not pass silently as a CS8785 or AD0001 warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. The change fixes the specific crash sites, but adds nothing in the product to surface unexpected exceptions in TypeCollector as an error or an error-level diagnostic. Any other unhandled case will still degrade to a warning and a missing resolver. Only the new tests guard against this.

refusals.reason: The README and MsgPack004 help page now document that diagnostics about members of types from referenced assemblies are never reported in the consuming project, which changes documented analyzer behaviour and is for the maintainers to approve.
